findings.name: Property Tax Benefit for 100% Disabled Veterans
findings.description: Idaho reduces property taxes by up to $1,500 on a home and up to one acre of land for veterans recognized as 100% service-connected disabled, or who receive 100% VA compensation due to individual unemployability, as of January 1 of the tax year. Applicants must own and reside in the Idaho home as their primary residence (with a current homeowner's exemption; mobile homes qualify) before April 15 of the qualifying year. There are no income requirements. Veterans in care facilities or nursing homes may still qualify. Applications are due between January 1 and April 15 each year via the Idaho State Tax Commission's online portal or a paper form to the county assessor, along with a current VA letter confirming the 100% disability rating; veterans with a VA "permanent and total" disability rating file once and the benefit renews automatically as long as residence doesn't change, while those without a permanent rating must reapply annually with a current rating letter. Solid waste, irrigation, and other government fees are excluded from the reduction.
findings.value: Up to $1,500 reduction in property taxes on home and up to one acre
otherReqs: 100% service-connected disability or 100% VA compensation for individual unemployability as of January 1
Own and reside in the Idaho home as primary residence before April 15
Current VA letter confirming disability rating required
Annual reapplication required unless VA rating is designated permanent and total
Application window January 1 - April 15
findings.agency: Idaho State Tax Commission / County Assessor
documentation: Current VA letter confirming 100% disability rating (or individual unemployability compensation)
Proof of homeowner's exemption on the primary residence
findings.sourceExcerpt: To qualify, you must be recognized as a veteran with a 100% service-connected disability or receive 100% compensation due to individual unemployability by the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs as of January 1. Own and reside in an Idaho home as primary residence before April 15, with current homeowner's exemption. The program could reduce property taxes on your home and up to one acre by as much as $1,500.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran License Plate
findings.description: Idaho issues a Disabled Veteran license plate at no initial or renewal cost to honorably discharged veterans with a 100% service-connected disability rating. Separately, Idaho Code § 49-403 also waives the registration/reregistration fee for a motor vehicle owned by a veteran receiving VA compensation for 100% service-connected disability, or for specific qualifying disabilities (loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet, loss or permanent loss of use of one or both hands, or loss of sight/virtual blindness in both eyes). Veterans are limited to one set of Disabled Veteran plates and must provide a copy of their VA Benefit Summary Letter, obtained via a Disabled Veteran Plate Eligibility Letter requested from the VA Regional Office in Boise.
findings.value: No initial or renewal fee for the Disabled Veteran plate; registration fee waived for qualifying disabled veterans under Idaho Code 49-403
otherReqs: Honorable discharge
100% service-connected disability rating (or one of the specific enumerated disabilities under Idaho Code 49-403)
Limited to one set of Disabled Veteran plates
VA Benefit Summary Letter / Disabled Veteran Plate Eligibility Letter required
documentation: Disabled Veteran Plate Eligibility Letter from the VA Regional Office
findings.sourceExcerpt: The Idaho Disabled Veteran license plate is offered to honorably discharged Veterans who have a 100% service-connected disability rating. There are no initial fees or renewal fees for this license plate. No fee shall be charged for the registration or reregistration of a motor vehicle owned by a veteran receiving compensation from the veterans administration for 100% service-connected disability or for specific disabilities including loss or permanent loss of use of one or both feet, loss or permanent loss of use of one or both hands, or loss of sight in both eyes.

findings.name: Disabled Veteran Hunting & Fishing License Discounts
findings.description: Idaho residents who are disabled American veterans with a service-connected disability rating of 40% or greater can obtain a combination hunting and fishing license for a nominal fee (roughly $5.00-$5.75 for a full annual fishing credential), plus reduced-rate big game tags: deer $10.75, elk $16.50, bear $6.75, turkey $10.75. Disability documentation (VA Benefit Summary Letter, submitted to an Idaho Fish and Game Regional Office by mail, email, or in person) is only required for the initial application. Separately, Idaho Fish and Game distributes five complimentary big game tags annually (deer, elk, pronghorn, black bear, or mountain lion, excluding controlled hunts with fewer than 10 tags) to disabled veterans through qualified 501(c)(3)/501(c)(4)/501(c)(19) nonprofits or government agencies, prioritizing Idaho Division of Veterans Services-sponsored applicants (40%+ service-connected disability); this is a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity with a January 2-31 application window. Nonresident disabled American veterans with a 40%+ VA disability rating qualify for reduced-fee licenses and tags (e.g., DAV hunting with 3-day fishing license $31.75; deer tag $23.75; elk tag $39.75), limited to 500 deer tags and 300 elk tags annually.
findings.value: Resident combination hunting/fishing license ~$5.00-$5.75 plus reduced big-game tags (40%+ disability); free once-in-a-lifetime big game tag via nonprofit sponsorship; reduced nonresident DAV license/tag pricing
otherReqs: Service-connected disability rating of 40% or greater
VA Benefit Summary Letter/Disability Percentage Rating letter required (initial application only for residents)
Free big-game tag program limited to five tags annually, once-in-a-lifetime, via qualified nonprofit/agency sponsorship, application window January 2-31
findings.agency: Idaho Department of Fish and Game
documentation: VA Benefit Summary Letter or official VA Disability Percentage Rating letter (40%+ service-connected disability)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Resident disabled American veterans with a service-connected disability of at least 40% can obtain a combination hunting and fishing license. Five complimentary big game tags are distributed annually to disabled veterans through qualified nonprofit organizations; tags are eligible for deer, elk, pronghorn, black bear, or mountain lion hunts. Nonresident disabled American veterans qualify for discounted pricing when providing proof of a service-connected disability rating of 40% or greater.

findings.name: State/Local Employment Veterans' Preference
findings.description: Idaho grants veterans' preference for state, county, city, and local public-employer positions (including taxing districts for sewers, roads, schools, and cemeteries): qualified veterans discharged under honorable or general conditions after at least 180 days of service receive a five-percentage-point increase to their earned civil service rating; veterans with a 10%+ service-connected disability receive a ten-percentage-point increase; and veterans with a 30%+ service-connected disability are entitled to an interview if they meet all position qualifications. Preference is also available to Purple Heart recipients and to spouses, widows, or widowers of honorably discharged preference-eligible veterans. Preference applies only to initial appointment, not to internal promotions, transfers, reassignments, second positions with the same employer, key/elected positions, or temporary/casual positions.
findings.value: 5 percentage-point rating increase (veterans); 10 percentage-point increase (10%+ disabled veterans); guaranteed interview (30%+ disabled veterans meeting qualifications)
otherReqs: Discharge under honorable or general conditions after at least 180 days of service
10-point-equivalent preference requires 10%+ service-connected disability
Interview guarantee requires 30%+ service-connected disability and meeting all position qualifications
Applies to initial appointment only, not promotions/transfers/reassignments
findings.agency: Idaho Department of Labor / Idaho Division of Human Resources
documentation: DD-214 or proof of honorable/general discharge
VA documentation of disability rating (for enhanced preference)
findings.sourceExcerpt: Veterans' Preference applies to positions with state, county, city, and local public employers. Qualified veterans receive a five percentage point increase to the rating otherwise earned. A veteran with a 10% service-connected disability receives an enhanced preference of a ten percentage point increase to their earned rating. A veteran with a 30% service-connected disability is entitled to an interview if they possess all the qualifications for the position.

findings.name: Armed Forces and Public Safety Officer (PSO) Dependent Scholarship
findings.description: Idaho's Armed Forces and Public Safety Officer Dependent Scholarship, administered through Next Steps Idaho, provides a waiver of tuition and fees, plus up to $750 per semester for books, and on-campus housing and subsistence, for undergraduate dependents of service members or public safety officers who were killed or became permanently disabled in the line of duty. The scholarship applies at Idaho public colleges and universities, including community colleges and four-year institutions.
findings.value: Waiver of tuition and fees, up to $750/semester for books, plus on-campus housing and subsistence
otherReqs: Applicant must be an undergraduate dependent of a service member or public safety officer killed or permanently disabled in the line of duty
Apply through the Next Steps Idaho scholarship portal
findings.agency: Idaho Division of Veterans Services / Next Steps Idaho
documentation: Proof of qualifying service member's/officer's death or permanent disability in the line of duty
findings.sourceExcerpt: The Armed Forces and Public Safety Officer (PSO) Dependent Scholarship provides a waiver of tuition and fees plus up to $750 per semester for books in addition to on-campus housing and subsistence. Designed for children of service members who were killed or became permanently disabled in the line of duty.

findings.name: Idaho State Veterans Homes (Boise, Lewiston, Pocatello, Post Falls)
findings.description: Idaho operates four state veterans homes (Boise, Lewiston, Pocatello, and Post Falls) providing nursing care to veterans who can no longer care for themselves. Eligibility requires proof of honorable military service (DD-214) showing a minimum of 90 days of active duty, or an earlier honorable discharge due to a service-connected disability; the veteran must be an Idaho resident at the time of admission. Spouses, widows, or widowers of an eligible veteran may also qualify for nursing care with proof of the veteran's honorable service and proof of marriage or a death certificate. Admission forms are available from the Home, a County or State Service Officer, or online; a State Service Officer assigned to each home reviews VA benefit eligibility and assists with the application, including Medicaid applications where relevant.
findings.value: Nursing care and supportive services for veterans and eligible spouses/widows/widowers
otherReqs: DD-214 or Military Discharge showing minimum 90 days active-duty honorable service (or earlier honorable discharge due to service-connected disability)
Idaho residency at time of admission
Spouses/widows/widowers require proof of the veteran's honorable service plus proof of marriage or a death certificate
findings.form: Idaho State Veterans Home Application for Admission
documentation: Proof of marriage/death certificate (for spouse/widow(er) applicants)
findings.sourceExcerpt: The Idaho Division of Veterans Services operates four Veterans Homes in Boise, Lewiston, Pocatello, and Post Falls. Applicants for nursing care must be a veteran (wartime or peacetime) or the spouse, widow, or widower of a veteran eligible for admission to a Home, with proof of honorable service in the United States Military (DD214 or Military Discharge) showing a minimum of 90 days active-duty service. Applicants must be a resident of the State of Idaho at the time of admission to a Home.
